title: Authority of Christ
definition: The authority of Christ is His divine right to teach, command, forgive, judge, rule, save, and send His people.
summary: Jesus speaks and acts with divine authority.
christFocus: Christ's authority is revealed in His teaching, miracles, forgiveness, lordship, and resurrection.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus' authority is evident throughout the Gospels. He teaches with authority, commands nature, forgives sins, casts out demons, raises the dead, and sends His disciples.

His authority is not borrowed from human institutions. It is divine authority belonging to Him as Son of God and risen Lord.

Because Christ has all authority, His people are called to trust His Word and obey His mission.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often treat Jesus as optional advisor rather than authoritative Lord. The authority of Christ matters because He has the right to command every life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Submit to Christ's authority in Scripture. Let His commands guide your choices and His mission direct your service.
